narrative.overview: The site is a frame; the work is the wall. The frame (navigation, text, panels, footer) stays neutral and quiet, with exactly one soft accent, so that the colour on the page is the colour of the projects.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral surfaces with ink-black text; one pink accent for the single call to action and focus.
Two typefaces only: Figtree Bold for display, Inter Regular for everything else.
Almost flat: one shadow, on the floating language switch.
Small radius (4px) everywhere, 8px only on the layered project ticket.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Pink marks the single action and the focus state. If a second thing on a screen is pink, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Real Colour Rule
rules.body: Interface colour never competes with project colour.

rules.name: The Text Grey Rule
rules.body: Text is Ink or Slate, never a lighter grey.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Figtree for structure, Inter for everything else. No third family.

rules.name: The No-Scaling Rule
rules.body: Text keeps its approved size per profile; layouts reflow around it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest except the language switch.

dos: Do keep the interface neutral and let the projects carry colour.
Do use Soft Orchid Pink only for the one call to action and for focus.
Do keep text at its approved size per profile and let layouts reflow around it.
Do keep every tap target at 44px or more and every focus state visible.
Do crop images with a focus point so faces stay in view, and keep readable text as text, never inside an image.
Do give French and English the same facts, layout and visual weight.
donts: Don't introduce a third typeface or a new colour; extend the existing tokens or ask first.
Don't use greys lighter than Slate for text.
Don't change a link's colour on hover; weight or opacity is the signal.
Don't add shadows, thick black lines, numbering or decorative borders to the interface.
Don't scale text with the viewport to make a composition fit.
Don't fabricate facts, figures, clients or quotes in case studies; leave the gap instead.
